title: Introduce cost-optimizer hint-proxy and quant-safety scanner with CLI wizard
author: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: Adds a lightweight 'cost-hint-proxy' service that surfaces tenant-specific batching/caching defaults and exposes a local API used by a new CLI 'redwood econ-wizard'. Also introduces a 'quant-safety-scanner' static checker that flags quantization profiles likely to regress unit economics or cause unacceptable latency spikes. Motivation: customers need safer automated defaults for batch/cache/quant settings and a low-friction operator tool to preview economic impact before rolling changes. This unblocks safer autopilot-style defaults for Dedicated/Private deployments while reducing manual ops overhead. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1842), [x] unit tests for scanner heuristics, [x] e2e smoke against a small local runtime, [x] CLI help/man page, [x] docs/operational cost playbook update. Commits: 6 commits (initial service scaffold; implement hint caching layer; add quant-safety heuristics; CLI wizard and dry-run mode; tests and fixtures; docs and changelog). Files changed (high level): packages/econ-proxy/{server,api,store}.go - new service and API; runtime/batcher/heuristics.go - wire hint lookups into scheduler; runtime/cache/policy.go - default cache TTL heuristics and tenant override logic; tools/cli/econ-wizard/ - new interactive CLI with dry-run export; tools/cli/tests - CLI unit tests; tools/quant-safety/scanner.py - static scanner used in CI and by CLI; docs/ops/cost-automation.md - operational guidance and examples; examples/econ-wizard-templates - tenant templates and sample outputs. Tests/CI: initial run had a lint failure (flake8 rule on scanner) which was fixed in commit 4; unit tests added for four canonical workload shapes; CI now green. Review convo: Diego requested clearer semantics for 'hint precedence' between tenant policy, global defaults, and transient sampling overrides; response added explicit precedence table to docs and enforced ordering in the proxy. Lena asked for a conservative default for the quant-safety thresholds and a bypass flag for migration windows; we added --unsafe-approve for controlled rollouts and lowered threshold aggressiveness. Owen suggested moving a noisy metric to debug level; moved metric and added a trace event for the scheduler warmup path. Risk analysis: scanner uses a conservative rule set derived from historical telemetry (unit cost delta > 7% OR p99 token latency > 1.5x baseline triggers a warning). The CLI produces a JSON 'dry-run' that includes estimated tokens/hour, expected cost delta, and recommended safe quant levels. Migration plan: ship as non-default behind a feature flag 'econ.hint_proxy.enabled' on main; enable rollout to staging tenants for 2 weeks, collect telemetry, then flip default for free-trial and self-serve accounts. Release notes: Adds econ-wizard CLI for previewing batch/cache/quant changes, a cost-hint-proxy service that centralizes tenant defaults, and a quant-safety-scanner that helps prevent destructive quantization rollouts. Merge: squash-merge after approvals and green CI. Related: touches runtime batching, dedicated autoscaler docs, and the private installer (small config flag).

notes: Feature flag default: disabled on main; enable via helm value econ.hint_proxy.enabled=true for staging tenants.
Follow-ups: telemetry aggregation for hint effectiveness (ENG-1901), add UI in Console for previewing econ-wizard results (PM backlog).
Hotfix plan: if any tenant sees increased p99 after rollout, the runtime will auto-fallback to previous quant/profile within 30s using 'graceful-degrade' policy.
